question: Can the pinned original Cano procedural generator be acquired and run without modifying its tracked source to produce at most one native topology/point-cloud/mesh smoke with traceable provenance?
method: Use an isolated checkout of https://github.com/LorenzoCanoAn/procedural-subt-gen at refactor commit b6c77621187404b4dfab1249c7a1b40f63ad9ab3. Audit repository identity, all license and dependency manifests, entry points, and seed behavior before creating an isolated Python environment. Then execute scripts/snippet_2.py directly and unmodified for at most one native smoke. Preserve raw logs, hashes, environment, native outputs, and failures. Do not write an adapter or alter third-party core in this run.
baseline: The repository and expected source files were remotely verified, but there is no local pinned checkout, no native Cano world bundle, and no reproducible executability evidence in the project.

user_authorization.scope: Execute the unique next task in docs/PLAN.md and docs/PROGRESS.md: acquire only the pinned Cano commit into isolated external storage, audit license and dependencies, run scripts/snippet_2.py unmodified, and preserve at most one native TNG/point-cloud/mesh smoke. Do not batch, adapt, import to Isaac, sample LiDAR, label, train, or modify M-TARE.
user_authorization.confirmation_reference: User message after providing Final Execution Plan V1 and requesting continued work: 开始干吧

acceptance_criteria: The isolated checkout remote and HEAD exactly match the frozen URL and commit, and no pre-existing target directory is overwritten.

All repository license notices and dependency manifests are inventoried. If no explicit license exists, integration, modification, redistribution, and open-source claims remain blocked even if local execution succeeds.
The original scripts/snippet_2.py tracked blob and filesystem hash are recorded before and after execution and remain unchanged; no tracked third-party file changes are permitted.
At most one native generation attempt is made and scripts/snippet_2.py exits successfully without changing its source.

Any native TNG, point-cloud, spline, or mesh products emitted by the original code are copied into the run artifacts with hashes; missing export products are reported as a failed criterion rather than silently repaired with an adapter.
The seed mechanism and repeatability claim are supported by original-source evidence; an absent or uncontrolled seed is reported and prevents a reproducibility PASS.
No batch map generation, first-party adapter, Isaac execution, LiDAR sampling, label generation, dataset construction, model training, ROS run, benchmark, or M-TARE modification occurs.
stop_conditions: Remote URL or commit does not match the frozen source
Dependency installation would require modifying tracked third-party source or a non-isolated system environment
Original snippet requires an interactive display and cannot complete headlessly without source modification
Original snippet raises an exception, hangs, or emits no auditable native output bundle
Any tracked third-party file changes during execution
More than one topology/world would be generated
expected_evidence: Pinned source provenance, repository status, commit metadata, file inventory, and tracked hashes
License audit and explicit allowed-use limitation
Dependency manifests, Python/platform details, isolated-environment package freeze, and installation logs
Original snippet stdout, stderr, exit code, duration, pre/post hash, and seed audit
At most one native TNG/point-cloud/spline/mesh artifact bundle with SHA-256 manifest
Scientifically relevant native graph/mesh preview only if produced without changing the original generator
Machine-readable summary with PASS, PARTIAL, FAIL, or BLOCKED per acceptance criterion

estimated_cost.compute: CPU-only repository acquisition, isolated Python dependency setup, and one native generator smoke; no GPU, Isaac, LiDAR, or training compute
